ukmt-grey-2016-03.title: Track the flips
ukmt-grey-2016-03.body:
Flipping about the lower edge puts the light grey triangle at the top and the dark grey triangle on the left. Flipping then about the right-hand edge swaps left and right, leaving light grey at the top and dark grey on the right.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-grey-2016-09.title: Compare perimeters
ukmt-grey-2016-09.body:
Let the cut-off triangles have sides $x,y,z$. The large triangle has side 20. The hexagon's perimeter is $40=60-(x+y+z)$, so $x+y+z=20$. The three small triangles have total perimeter $3(x+y+z)=60$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 60 cm**

ukmt-grey-2016-10.title: Write the sum
ukmt-grey-2016-10.body:
If the triplets are $x$ years old, Jon and Jim are $x-3$. The sum is $3x+2(x-3)=5x-6$, which is one less than a multiple of 5. Of the options only 89 fits ($x=19$).

**Answer: (D) 89**

ukmt-grey-2016-13.title: Count matches
ukmt-grey-2016-13.body:
The finalists each win three matches (quarter-final, semi-final, final). Only Glen (beat Harry, Carl, Ed) and Carl (beat Damian, Bart, ...) played the right number: Glen has three wins and Carl has two wins and one loss, so they met in the final.

**Answer: (A) Glen and Carl**

ukmt-grey-2016-23.title: Express the top number
ukmt-grey-2016-23.body:
Label the bottom layer $a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i$ (rows). The top number is $50+(b+d+f+h)+3e$. To maximise, make $e$ largest, so the other eight are the smallest $1,\dots,8$ and $e=50-36=14$. Then $b,d,f,h$ should be $5,6,7,8$, sum 26. Top $=50+26+42=118$.

**Answer: (D) 118**

ukmt-grey-2016-24.title: Neighbour counts
ukmt-grey-2016-24.body:
Let carriages hold $p,q,r,s,t$ passengers. A passenger in carriage 1 has $p-1+q$ neighbours, which is 5 or 10; in carriage 2, $p+q+r-1$. Since $r\ge1$ we get $p+q=6$ and $r=5$. By symmetry $s+t=6$. Total $6+5+6=17$.

**Answer: (C) 17**
